args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. v2.3.1 (and its staging candidate v2.3.1-rc) were both marked unhealthy. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying; note that v2.3.1-rc was already unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened incident INC-0001 at SEV2, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **The problem:** the latest release, v2.3.1, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run it, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** the summary covers the failure, the rollback and the post-rollback health numbers. It also says v2.3.1 needs a root-cause investigation before anyone redeploys it.

The test version of v2.3.1 was already marked unhealthy in staging before it went to production. That's worth a look in the follow-up: the warning sign was there and the release went out anyway.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
